answer: A lagoon of idle identities becomes expensive to flood when each agent must lock a refundable stake before it can transact. The stake is released only after peers attest to real completed work, and it is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicates. Reputation then accrues slowly toward a zenith that a fresh clone cannot fake, while every attestation leaves a crystal-clear, publicly verifiable audit trail. An attacker must pay the stake for every fake identity, so the cost of a sybil swarm grows linearly while its benefit stays flat.
